$schemaNote: Hardware -> Linux support. Used by `switchcheck linux`. First matching entry wins.

gpu.name: NVIDIA GPU
gpu.note: Works with the proprietary driver (preinstalled on Ubuntu; 'Additional Drivers' picks it). Two caveats: disable Secure Boot or enroll the MOK key it offers, and expect driver updates to lag kernel updates by days.
gpu.advice: Install via the distro's driver manager, not NVIDIA's .run file.

gpu.name: AMD GPU
gpu.note: Best-supported vendor on Linux: the in-kernel Mesa/RADV driver just works, including Vulkan. No install needed.
gpu.advice: For very new GPUs use the newest distro release for fresh Mesa.

gpu.name: Intel GPU
gpu.note: In-kernel Mesa driver, zero setup. Arc GPUs matured a lot; newest kernels/Mesa still recommended.

nic.name: Realtek NIC
nic.note: Most Realtek ethernet/wifi chips are supported in-tree; some USB wi-fi dongles (8812/8821 family) need DKMS out-of-tree drivers.
nic.advice: USB wi-fi dongle? Search the exact chip + 'linux dkms' before switching.

nic.name: Broadcom Wi-Fi
nic.note: Works, but needs proprietary firmware/brcm packages — the classic first-day-of-Linux headache on old MacBooks and cheap laptops.
nic.advice: Install broadcom-sta or brcm firmware packages from the live USB first.

nic.name: Qualcomm/MediaTek NIC
nic.note: ath9k/ath10k/ath11k and mt79xx are in-tree and generally fine.

nic.name: Wi-Fi adapter
nic.note: Modern wi-fi is well supported via in-tree drivers + linux-firmware; 6E/7 need recent kernels.
nic.advice: Run the newest LTS or rolling distro for the newest radios.

printer.name: HP printer
printer.note: First-class: HPLIP is preinstalled on major distros (printing + scanning).

printer.name: Brother printer
printer.note: Brother ships official Linux drivers (deb/rpm); driverless IPP also works on recent models.
printer.advice: Grab the .deb from Brother's site or use IPP Everywhere.

printer.name: Canon printer
printer.note: Canon publishes Linux drivers; scanning (scangearmp) is the flaky part. Recent models do driverless IPP.
printer.advice: Prefer the network/IPP path over USB for Canon.

printer.name: Epson printer
printer.note: escpr/escpr2 drivers in distro repos; Imagescan for scanners.

printer.name: Office printer
printer.note: All major office brands support IPP Everywhere / driverless printing on Linux today.
printer.advice: Add it as an IPP Everywhere printer and skip vendor drivers.

printer.name: Virtual printer
printer.note: Every desktop ships 'Print to File' (PDF) built in.

defaultPrinter.note: Modern printing is driverless (IPP Everywhere/AirPrint); unknown printers usually 'just work' over the network.
defaultPrinter.advice: Search '<model> linux' if it is a USB-only legacy device.
